text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall — Severity: P1 — Smart routing anomaly detected. Cost-based routing started sending significant traffic to low-cost variant 'gpt-lite-v2' in us-west-2. Multiple customer quality regressions flagged by QA + monitoring. Start: 2026-02-18T12:03:54Z. Autosilence threshold not hit. @oncall please respond.
Alex: I’m on it. grabbing logs and routing config now. any customer-facing impact yet?
Emily: Support here — we’ve got 3 escalation tickets flagged as hallucinations / malformed outputs from two enterprise customers (cust-452, cust-887). They started rolling in around 12:05 UTC.
Sara: Observability — spike in generation error rate and a drop in Rouge/QA metrics for the policy group that prefers cost. Dashboard: 
```
error_rate_by_model: gpt-lite-v2 +12% since 12:00
response_quality_score: gpt-lite-v2 -27% vs baseline
traffic_share: gpt-lite-v2 -> 63% (should be <= 10% for production)
```
Looks like routing weight suddenly increased.
Jordan: Who touched routing policy configs in the last 24h? I’ll check deploys.
Priya: I rolled a small change to the policy engine yesterday to add a new `cost_preference` field for experiments (PR 5248). It was behind a feature flag but I see the flag was flipped on in prod for us-west-2 at ~03:10 UTC. I am digging.
Alex: If cost_preference mistakenly got a high weight we could accidentally override quality heuristics. Can you paste the policy blob?
Priya: Pasting relevant snippet from the active policy (sanitized):
```
{
  "policy_id": "smart-routing-v3",
  "selectors": [...],
  "score_weights": {
    "latency": 0.2,
    "quality_estimate": 0.3,
    "cost_preference": 0.8   // <-- this looks wrong, should be 0.08
  }
}
```
That `0.8` is indeed the flipped param. I’m 90% sure the helm path default was wrong.
Alex: That explains it. Need an immediate mitigation — manual override to pin traffic for affected customers to `gpt-std-1` (higher-quality variant) while we fix policy.
EngRuntimeLead: Agreed. We have an internal route-override API. Use the emergency override endpoint to set model_preference for tenant groups. I’ll coordinate capacity.
Jordan: Oncall handoff — I’m taking over live coordination. Alex, Priya — please prepare a rollback/patch. Emily, Raj — collect impacted customer list & severity for postmortem.
Alex: Executing override now:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/route-override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EMERGENCY_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"selector": "tenant_group:enterprise", "model": "gpt-std-1", "ttl": 3600}'
```
Response: 200 OK. Override applied to enterprise group.
Sara: Metrics confirm enterprise traffic to gpt-std-1 jumped and quality metrics are recovering within two token windows. Good.
Emily: Notifying the two affected customers with interim message and mitigation steps. Asking them to validate outputs.
Priya: I’ll revert the feature flag immediately in us-west-2 and push corrected default weight. Preparing hotfix PR now (will target 5248-fix).
Jordan: Also ensure fallback loops aren’t created — we saw routing fallbacks in the logs where cheaper model was selected, failed quality checks, then fallback retried and hit same policy (loop). Need to add a guard.
Alex: Log snippet of fallback loop: 
```
2026-02-18T12:04:05Z route_select: selected=gpt-lite-v2 score=0.74
2026-02-18T12:04:05Z quality_check: failed threshold -> trigger_fallback
2026-02-18T12:04:05Z route_select: re-evaluated selected=gpt-lite-v2 (policy stable) -> loop
```
We should short-circuit repeated retries to prevent tight loops.
EngRuntimeLead: A quick mitigation: add transient blacklist for model per-request after a failed quality check for N seconds. I’ll open a ticket to rollout. For now set fallback retries = 0 in routing config.
Priya: Hotfix PR open -> merging after +1. Patch includes corrected weight and add a max_retry=0 fallback flag.
Jordan: PR merged. Deploying to us-west-2 now.
Sara: Deployment logs show new config applied at 12:22 UTC. Quality weights now: latency 0.2, quality_estimate 0.3, cost_preference 0.05.
Alex: Removing emergency override for enterprise now and letting policy decide (but with corrected weights).
Alex: `DELETE https://internal-api.redwood/v1/route-override?selector=tenant_group:enterprise` -> 200 OK.
Sara: Traffic redistribution looks healthy. gpt-lite-v2 traffic back down to ~8%. Quality metrics stable.
Emily: Customers confirmed better outputs; cust-452 closed their ticket, cust-887 marked as resolved. Sending follow-up emails with root-cause summary.
Raj: Capturing impacted customers list: cust-452 (enterprise, high), cust-887 (enterprise, med), cust-1291 (mid-market, low) — all saw quality drop but only first two escalated.
Jordan: Next steps checklist:
- Incident commander: Jordan (owns)
- Root cause: policy weight misconfigured + flag flip in prod -> cost preference dominated selection
- Immediate fix: route override, rollback flag, hotfix PR, disable retries
- Customer remediation: notifications + SLA credits eval by ops/finance
- Postmortem owner: Priya and Alex to co-author
- Timeline for fixes: regression alerts + canary of routing changes -> 48h
Priya: I’ll prep postmortem draft and include tests to prevent shipping a cost weight >0.2 without explicit approval.
EngRuntimeLead: Also adding an integration test to the policy engine that fails CI if cost_preference > 0.5 for any prod rollout.
Alex: Any outstanding items?
Emily: Ask PMs about proactively contacting top affected accounts. I’ll coordinate with Raj.
Jordan: Closing on-call: moving to watch mode for 2h. If anything spikes, re-open thread. Thanks all for fast response. :thumbsup: 
IncidentBot: Incident resolved -> severity downgraded to P3. Final note: mitigation completed, customers notified, postmortem assigned.
